words: One pig almost started a war between America and Britain.
label: ONE PIG

words: Not because it attacked someone important.
label: NOT AN ATTACK
visual: pig illustration; chalk-write NOT AN ATTACK

words: Not because it carried secret information.
label: NO SECRETS

words: It simply ate the wrong potatoes.
label: POTATOES

words: And within weeks, American soldiers were landing on an island,
label: SOLDIERS LAND

words: British warships were gathering offshore,
label: WARSHIPS

words: and two powerful nations were preparing for a possible battle.
label: TWO NATIONS

words: All because one farmer had lost his patience.
label: ONE ANGRY FARMER
visual: pig illustration; chalk-write ONE ANGRY FARMER

words: This is the true story of the Pig War.
label: THE PIG WAR
visual: pig illustration; chalk-write THE PIG WAR

words: The island nobody could agree on.
label: WHO OWNS THE ISLAND?
visual: map illustration; chalk-write WHO OWNS THE ISLAND?

words: To understand how this happened,
label: A BORDER DISPUTE
visual: map illustration; chalk-write A BORDER DISPUTE

words: we need to go back to 1846.
America and Britain signed a treaty establishing much of their border in the Pacific Northwest.
label: A TREATY

words: But there was one problem.
label: ONE PROBLEM

words: The treaty said the border should pass through the channel between the mainland and Vancouver Island.
label: WHICH CHANNEL?

words: Except, there were two possible channels.
label: TWO CHANNELS

words: Choose the western channel, and the San Juan Islands belonged to America.
label: WEST: AMERICA

words: Choose the eastern channel, and they belonged to Britain.
label: EAST: BRITAIN

words: Naturally, both countries chose the version that gave them the islands.
label: COMPETING CLAIMS

words: And neither wanted to back down.
label: NEITHER BACKS DOWN
visual: map illustration; chalk-write NEITHER BACKS DOWN

words: The farmer and the pig.
label: THE FARMER + THE PIG
visual: farm illustration; chalk-write THE FARMER + THE PIG

words: By 1859, the British Hudson's Bay Company was operating a large sheep farm on San Juan Island.
label: 1859: SHEEP FARM

words: American settlers were also arriving,
label: AMERICAN SETTLERS

words: building houses and planting crops.
label: HOUSES + CROPS

words: Both sides believed the other was trespassing.
label: TRESPASSING?

words: Then came June 15th, 1859.
label: JUNE 15, 1859

words: An American farmer named Lyman Cutlar discovered a pig digging through his potato patch.
label: LYMAN CUTLAR

words: And this wasn't the pig's first visit.
label: NOT ITS FIRST VISIT
visual: farm illustration; chalk-write NOT ITS FIRST VISIT

words: The animal belonged to Charles Griffin,
label: CHARLES GRIFFIN

words: a British company farm manager.
label: BRITISH FARM MANAGER
visual: farm illustration; chalk-write BRITISH FARM MANAGER

words: Cutlar had finally had enough.
label: ENOUGH!

words: In a moment of anger,
label: ANGER

words: he shot the pig.
label: THE PIG IS SHOT
visual: farm illustration; chalk-write THE PIG IS SHOT

words: But he had no idea what he had just started.
label: AN UNEXPECTED CRISIS
visual: farm illustration; chalk-write AN UNEXPECTED CRISIS

words: A hundred dollar pig.
label: A $100 PIG?

words: Cutlar soon regretted his decision.
label: REGRET

words: He approached Griffin and offered to compensate him for the animal.
label: COMPENSATION

words: But there was a disagreement.
label: A DISAGREEMENT

words: Cutlar believed the pig was worth no more than ten dollars.
Griffin demanded one hundred dollars,
ten times as much.
label: 10 TIMES AS MUCH
visual: money illustration; chalk-write 10 TIMES AS MUCH

words: Cutlar refused.
label: REFUSAL

words: Then British officials threatened to arrest him.
label: THREAT OF ARREST
visual: money illustration; chalk-write THREAT OF ARREST

words: But Cutlar insisted he was an American citizen living on American soil.
label: AMERICAN SOIL?

words: The British insisted the island belonged to
label: A BRITISH CLAIM
visual: money illustration; chalk-write A BRITISH CLAIM

words: Britain.
label: BRITAIN

words: And suddenly, a disagreement about one pig
label: ONE PIG

words: had become an international dispute.
label: INTERNATIONAL DISPUTE

words: The warships arrive.
label: THE WARSHIPS ARRIVE
visual: military illustration; chalk-write THE WARSHIPS ARRIVE

words: Worried American settlers asked the United States Army for protection.
label: PROTECTION

words: General William Harney responded by sending soldiers to the island.
label: GENERAL HARNEY

words: Their commander was Captain George Pickett.
label: CAPTAIN PICKETT

words: The same Pickett who would later become infamous during the American Civil War.
label: BEFORE THE CIVIL WAR
visual: military illustration; chalk-write BEFORE THE CIVIL WAR

words: In July, American troops landed and established a military camp.
label: JULY: AMERICAN CAMP
visual: military illustration; chalk-write JULY: AMERICAN CAMP

words: The British were furious.
label: BRITISH ANGER

words: Governor James Douglas ordered British warships toward the island.
label: GOVERNOR DOUGLAS

words: The Americans refused to leave.
label: AMERICANS STAY

words: The British refused to surrender their claim.
label: BRITAIN HOLDS ITS CLAIM
visual: military illustration; chalk-write BRITAIN HOLDS ITS CLAIM

words: More soldiers arrived.
label: MORE SOLDIERS

words: More ships appeared.
label: MORE SHIPS

words: By the end of August, hundreds of American troops were positioned behind defenses with cannons.
label: HUNDREDS + CANNONS

words: British naval forces waited offshore.
label: BRITISH NAVY

words: One wrong decision could have turned this little island into a battlefield.
label: ONE WRONG DECISION
visual: military illustration; chalk-write ONE WRONG DECISION

words: The world almost went to war.
label: ALMOST A WAR
visual: military illustration; chalk-write ALMOST A WAR

words: But something strange was happening.
label: AN UNEXPECTED TWIST
visual: peace illustration; chalk-write AN UNEXPECTED TWIST

words: Even as both sides prepared for possible fighting,
label: PREPARING TO FIGHT
visual: peace illustration; chalk-write PREPARING TO FIGHT

words: officers sometimes visited each other.
label: OFFICERS VISIT

words: Some even attended church services together.
label: CHURCH TOGETHER

words: They were behaving like neighbors while preparing to fight like enemies.
label: NEIGHBORS + ENEMIES

words: Fortunately, British Rear Admiral Lambert Baynes understood the danger.
label: ADMIRAL BAYNES

words: He refused to turn a dispute over a pig into a war between two nations.
label: NO WAR OVER A PIG
visual: peace illustration; chalk-write NO WAR OVER A PIG

words: Meanwhile, American President James Buchanan learned what was happening.
label: PRESIDENT BUCHANAN

words: He was alarmed.
label: ALARM

words: He sent General Winfield Scott to calm the situation.
label: WINFIELD SCOTT

words: And Scott helped negotiate a compromise.
label: A COMPROMISE

words: Neither country would take complete control.
label: NO SOLE CONTROL
visual: peace illustration; chalk-write NO SOLE CONTROL

words: Both would remain on the island until the border dispute could be settled peacefully.
label: A PEACEFUL SOLUTION
visual: peace illustration; chalk-write A PEACEFUL SOLUTION

words: Thirteen years of waiting.
label: 13 YEARS

words: So, the Americans remained at American Camp.
label: AMERICAN CAMP

words: The British established English Camp at the other end of the island.
label: ENGLISH CAMP

words: And they waited.
label: WAITING

words: Not for days, not for months.
label: NOT DAYS OR MONTHS
visual: camps illustration; chalk-write NOT DAYS OR MONTHS

words: The joint military occupation continued for twelve more years.
label: 12 MORE YEARS

words: Think about that.
label: THINK ABOUT THAT
visual: camps illustration; chalk-write THINK ABOUT THAT

words: The pig was long gone.
label: THE PIG IS LONG GONE
visual: camps illustration; chalk-write THE PIG IS LONG GONE

words: The original argument had become history.
label: THE ARGUMENT IS HISTORY
visual: camps illustration; chalk-write THE ARGUMENT IS HISTORY

words: But British and American troops were still occupying the same small island, waiting for someone to decide who owned it.
label: STILL SHARING AN ISLAND
visual: camps illustration; chalk-write STILL SHARING AN ISLAND

words: Finally, in 1871, both countries agreed to let Germany's Kaiser Wilhelm the First arbitrate the dispute.
label: 1871: ARBITRATION

words: The final decision.
label: THE FINAL DECISION
visual: verdict illustration; chalk-write THE FINAL DECISION

words: In October 1872, the decision finally arrived.
label: OCTOBER 1872

words: The San Juan Islands belonged to America.
label: ISLANDS TO AMERICA
visual: verdict illustration; chalk-write ISLANDS TO AMERICA

words: British troops withdrew.
label: BRITISH WITHDRAWAL

words: The crisis was over.
label: CRISIS OVER

words: Thirteen years after a pig wandered into a potato patch,
label: 1859 TO 1872

words: two of the world's most powerful nations had finally settled their argument.
label: DISPUTE SETTLED

words: No battle had taken place.
label: NO BATTLE

words: Not a single human was killed in the confrontation.
label: 0 HUMAN DEATHS

words: And the only casualty of the entire Pig War?
label: THE ONLY CASUALTY?
visual: end illustration; chalk-write THE ONLY CASUALTY?

words: The pig.
label: ONE PIG

words: All because it wanted some potatoes.
label: SOME POTATOES
